lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Paul blesses God as the Father of mercies, who comforts us in trouble so that we can comfort others, and tells of a deadly trouble in Asia that taught him to trust in God who raises the dead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God comforts us, using 2 Corinthians 1:3-4?
ev: Say who God is called in 1:3
Explain why we are comforted (1:4)
Explain what Paul learned from the trouble in Asia (1:8-10)

nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Corinthians: comfort in affliction, the ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation, the collection for the saints, and a defence of his apostleship (1:1-13:14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 2 Corinthians and say what its three main parts are about?
ev: Name the main sections: comfort and ministry (1-7), the collection (8-9), Paul's defence of his apostleship (10-13)
Say what Paul tells the Corinthians about his sufferings

nodes.t: All God's promises are yes in Christ
nodes.d: Paul defends changing his travel plans, saying his word is not yes and no, because God is true and in Christ all the promises of God are yes; God has established, anointed and sealed believers and given the Spirit as a guarantee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that all the promises of God are yes in Christ (2 Corinthians 1:20)?
ev: Explain what Paul says about God's promises in 1:20
List what God has done for believers in 1:21-22
Say why Paul had not yet come to Corinth (1:23)

nodes.d: Paul says he wrote with many tears, that the punishment the majority inflicted on the offender is enough, and urges the church to forgive and comfort him so that Satan gets no advantage.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul urges the Corinthians to forgive and comfort the man who had been punished (2 Corinthians 2:5-11)?
ev: Say why Paul wrote with tears (2:4)
Explain what Paul asks the church to do for the punished man (2:7-8)
Say why forgiving matters (2:11)

nodes.t: Led in triumph: the fragrance of Christ
nodes.d: After telling of his restlessness at Troas, Paul thanks God who leads us in triumph in Christ and spreads the knowledge of him, which is a fragrance of life to some and of death to others.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by being a sweet savour of Christ, using 2 Corinthians 2:14-17?
ev: Explain the two kinds of aroma in 2:15-16
Contrast Paul's speaking with those who corrupt the word of God (2:17)

nodes.d: Paul says the Corinthians are Christ's letter written by the Spirit on hearts, calls himself a minister of the new testament, and contrasts the ministry of death carved on stone, with its fading glory, with the ministry of the Spirit and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul contrasts the ministry written on stone with the ministry of the Spirit in 2 Corinthians 3:3-11?
ev: Say what the Corinthians are called in 3:2-3
Explain the difference between the letter and the Spirit (3:6)
Compare the two ministrations in 3:7-11

nodes.t: Unveiled face: from glory to glory
nodes.d: Paul says Moses put a veil over his face, a veil that remains in the reading of the old testament but is done away in Christ, and that believers with open face behold the glory of the Lord and are changed into his image.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happens to a person who turns to the Lord, using 2 Corinthians 3:16-18?
ev: Explain the veil of Moses (3:13-15)
Say when the veil is taken away (3:16)
Explain what happens to those who behold the Lord's glory (3:18)

nodes.d: Paul says the gospel is the light of the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Christ, hidden to those blinded by the god of this world, and that believers carry it in weak earthen vessels so that the power is God's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says we have this treasure in earthen vessels (2 Corinthians 4:7)?
ev: Explain who blinds unbelievers and why (4:4)
Say where the light of the knowledge of God's glory is seen (4:6)
Explain why we have the treasure in earthen vessels (4:7)
Describe the four contrasts in 4:8-9

nodes.d: Paul says that although the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day, and that light affliction produces an eternal weight of glory for those who look at the unseen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul does not lose heart, using 2 Corinthians 4:16-18?
ev: Contrast the outward and inward man (4:16)
Contrast the seen and the unseen (4:18)

nodes.t: The heavenly house and the judgment seat
nodes.d: Paul says that if the earthly tent is destroyed, believers have an eternal house from God, are confident to be present with the Lord, walk by faith, and must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about being at home with the Lord and about the judgment seat in 2 Corinthians 5:1-10?
ev: Say what Paul expects after the tent is dissolved (5:1)
Explain what Paul says about walking by faith (5:7)
Say who must appear before Christ's judgment seat (5:10)

nodes.t: New creation and the ministry of reconciliation
nodes.d: Paul says the love of Christ constrains us because he died for all, that anyone in Christ is a new creature, that God reconciled us in Christ and gave us the message of reconciliation, and that Christ was made sin for us so that we might become the righteousness of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be reconciled to God, using 2 Corinthians 5:18-21?
ev: Explain why Christ died for all (5:15)
Say what is true of anyone in Christ (5:17)
Explain reconciliation in 5:18-19
Explain the exchange described in 5:21

nodes.t: Now is the day of salvation: marks of true ministry
nodes.d: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive God's grace in vain, says now is the day of salvation, and lists the hardships and virtues by which he commends himself as a minister of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by "now is the day of salvation" in 2 Corinthians 6:2?
ev: Quote the point of 6:2
List some hardships in 6:4-5 and some virtues in 6:6-7
Explain the paradoxes in 6:8-10

nodes.t: Separation and the temple of the living God
nodes.d: Paul warns against being unequally yoked with unbelievers, says believers are the temple of the living God, and gives promises that God will be their Father and they his sons and daughters, calling them to cleanse themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says believers should not be unequally yoked with unbelievers, using 2 Corinthians 6:14-18?
ev: Name the contrasts Paul draws in 6:14-16
Say what promises are given in 6:16-18
Explain the conclusion of 7:1

nodes.d: Paul tells how Titus comforted him in Macedonia with news of the Corinthians' repentance, and distinguishes godly sorrow, which leads to repentance and salvation, from the sorrow of the world which brings death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference between godly sorrow and worldly sorrow, using 2 Corinthians 7:9-11?
ev: State the difference between godly sorrow and the sorrow of the world (7:10)
Say who brought comfort and what he reported (7:6-7)
List fruits of the Corinthians' sorrow (7:11)

nodes.t: The grace of giving: the churches of Macedonia
nodes.d: Paul tells of the Macedonians' generous gift out of deep poverty, urges the Corinthians to complete their part, points to Christ who became poor so that we might be rich, and says the aim is fairness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Christ's example motivates giving, using 2 Corinthians 8:9?
ev: Describe the Macedonians' giving (8:2-5)
Explain Christ's example in 8:9
Say what Paul means by equality in 8:13-15

nodes.t: Titus and the brothers: honesty with the offering
nodes.d: Paul commends Titus and two brothers sent to administer the gift, so that no one could blame him and everything would be honest before the Lord and men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul arranged for several trusted men to handle the offering (2 Corinthians 8:20-21)?
ev: Name who is sent to Corinth (8:16-23)
Explain why Paul takes care to be honest about the gift (8:20-21)

nodes.d: Paul urges the Corinthians to be ready with the gift, saying that he who sows bountifully will reap bountifully, that each should give as he has decided in his heart, and that God supplies all they need and receives thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how God wants us to give, using 2 Corinthians 9:6-8?
ev: Say how each person should give (9:7)
Explain the sowing and reaping picture (9:6)
Say what the gift produces according to 9:12-13

nodes.d: Paul says he does not war according to the flesh, that his weapons are mighty to pull down strongholds and bring every thought captive to Christ, and answers those who say his presence is weak.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about the weapons of our warfare in 2 Corinthians 10:3-5?
ev: Explain what the weapons of Paul's warfare do (10:4-5)
Say what critics said about Paul (10:10)
Say what authority the Lord gave him for (10:8)

nodes.d: Paul says he will not compare himself with those who commend themselves or boast of others' work; his boasting stays within the limit God assigned, and the one approved is the one the Lord commends.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is truly approved, using 2 Corinthians 10:17-18?
ev: Explain the limit Paul keeps in his boasting (10:13-16)
Quote the principle of 10:17-18

nodes.t: False apostles and Paul's foolish boasting
nodes.d: Paul fears the Corinthians will be led astray from Christ as the serpent deceived Eve, warns of false apostles disguised as servants of righteousness, and, speaking as a fool, lists his sufferings as a servant of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul warns about false apostles in 2 Corinthians 11:13-15 and why he lists his sufferings?
ev: Say what Paul fears in 11:3
Explain how false apostles disguise themselves (11:13-15)
List some sufferings Paul names in 11:23-27
Describe the escape at Damascus (11:32-33)

nodes.t: The thorn in the flesh: power in weakness
nodes.d: Paul tells of being caught up to paradise, then of a thorn in the flesh given to keep him humble; the Lord answered his prayer by saying his grace is sufficient and his strength is made perfect in weakness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says "when I am weak, then am I strong," using 2 Corinthians 12:7-10?
ev: Say what Paul asked the Lord three times (12:8)
Quote the Lord's answer (12:9)
Explain why Paul can say he is strong when weak (12:10)

nodes.t: Paul's signs, his love and his fears
nodes.d: Paul says the signs of an apostle were done among the Corinthians, that he will not burden them but gladly spend himself for them, and that he fears finding sin and disorder when he comes a third time.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would not burden the Corinthians, using 2 Corinthians 12:14-15?
ev: Say how Paul describes his care for them (12:14-15)
List the sins Paul fears finding (12:20-21)

nodes.t: Examine yourselves: final warnings and blessing
nodes.d: Paul warns that he will not spare those who have sinned, tells the Corinthians to examine themselves whether they are in the faith, and closes with an exhortation and a trinitarian blessing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul asks the Corinthians to do in 2 Corinthians 13:5 and name the three persons in 13:14?
ev: Quote the command of 13:5
Name the three persons in the blessing of 13:14
List the closing exhortations in 13:11

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: God creates the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them, in six days, and rests on the seventh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God made on each day, and what happened on the seventh?
ev: Retell what God made on each of the six days
Say that God rested on the seventh day and blessed it

nodes.d: The serpent tempts the woman; she and the man eat the fruit God forbade and hide from God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how sin entered the world in Genesis 3?
ev: Retell the temptation and the disobedience in order
Explain what the man and woman did when God called

nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.t: Moses asks to see God's glory
nodes.d: Moses asks that God's presence go with them and then to see his glory. The LORD says his presence will go with Moses, that he will make all his goodness pass and proclaim his name, but no man can see his face and live; Moses is hidden in a cleft of the rock and sees only his back.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Moses asked to see and how God answered?
ev: Say what Moses asked in 33:15 and 33:18
Say what God said he would do and what he would not allow (33:19-23)

nodes.d: Moses hews two new tablets and goes up Sinai, where the LORD descends in the cloud and proclaims his name as merciful, gracious, longsuffering and abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity yet not clearing the guilty. Moses bows and asks God to go among them and pardon their sin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the LORD described himself in 34:6-7 and what Moses asked?
ev: List words from 34:6-7 that describe the LORD
Say what Moses asked in 34:9

nodes.d: Moses comes down with the two tablets and does not know that the skin of his face shines; Aaron and Israel are afraid to come near. Moses speaks to them and wears a veil over his face except when he goes in before the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened to Moses' face and when he wore a veil?
ev: Say why people were afraid to come near (34:30)
Say when Moses took the veil off (34:34)

nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: I have redeemed you; I am the LORD, your Saviour
nodes.d: The LORD redeems and calls Jacob by name, will be with them through waters and fire, gathers sons from the ends of the earth, calls Israel his witnesses, does a new thing, and blots out their transgressions for his own sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Isaiah 43:1-2 and 43:25?
ev: Quote the promise in Isaiah 43:1-2
Say what Israel is called in 43:10-12
Explain the "new thing" (43:18-19) and the forgiveness in 43:25

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: A prayer of remembrance and lament
nodes.d: The prophet recalls the LORD's kindnesses and how Israel rebelled and he became their enemy, then prays for him to look down and come down, confessing sin, and says "we are the clay and thou our potter."
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the prayer of Isaiah 63:15-64:12 and what the people confess?
ev: Recall what the LORD did for his people (63:7-14)
Quote the confession in 64:6
Quote 64:8

nodes.d: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth, receives the word of the LORD from the thirteenth year of Josiah to the exile after Zedekiah's eleventh year, warning Judah of judgment from the north and promising restoration and a new covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jeremiah was and during whose reigns the word of the LORD came to him according to Jeremiah 1:1-3?
ev: Name the kings during whose reigns the word came (Jeremiah 1:1-3)
Explain that the book is not arranged only in the order of the events it describes, using examples from its dates

nodes.d: The LORD promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah, unlike the one broken after the exodus: he will write his law on their hearts, they will all know him, and he will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what is new about the covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31-34?
ev: Say whom the covenant is made with and what it is unlike (31:31-32)
Describe what the LORD does in 31:33
Quote the promise of forgiveness in 31:34
